Definition: a primary verb; used only in certain past tenses, the others being borrowed from the equivalent G3700 and G3708; properly, to see (literally or figuratively); by implication, (in the perfect tense only) to know:--be aware, behold, X can (+ not tell), consider, (have) know(-ledge), look (on), perceive, see, be sure, tell, understand, wish, wot. Compare G3700.
BiblicalUsage: This is the old form of the verb to know or to see, and the Greek text carries it only as a form of the verb to know, spelled I might know. Paul says if he had all knowledge and understood all mysteries but had not love, he would be nothing, and he says that if he does not know the meaning of a voice, he will be a barbarian to the speaker. The word is rare, but the knowing it names is the heart of the passage.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe knowing without love is nothing, because Paul puts knowledge on trial and finds it empty without it.
